author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260513T041030Z-2473287
text:
Escalating again: after reading the spec, the bead text, and the existing handler together, there are three unreconciled issues that need a one-shot clarification before code lands.

## 1. Spec text is internally in tension

`draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md` §Space/query (lines 1175-1182):

> Line 1177: Standard JMAP `/query`.
> Line 1182: When the request includes an `isPublic: true` filter condition, servers MUST include Spaces for which the requesting account is not a member but which have `isPubliclyPreviewable: true`. For such non-member results, the server MUST return only the fields `id`, `name`, `description`, `iconBlobId`, `memberCount`, `createdAt`, `isPublic`, and `isPubliclyPreviewable`; all other fields MUST be omitted. For Spaces where the requesting account is a member, full Space objects are returned regardless of the filter.

"Standard JMAP `/query`" (RFC 8620 §5.5) returns only `ids[]`, no field values. Line 1182 talks about "return only the fields" and "full Space objects are returned" — which only makes sense if `/query` embeds objects (a deviation from RFC 8620 the spec text does not explicitly call out and for which no response-shape extension is defined).

Section §Space/get (line 1104-1106) is one line: "Standard JMAP `/get`." No mention of the non-member trim.

I read the chat-spec git log: `isPubliclyPreviewable` landed in commit 20a7b81 (initial drop) and has not been touched since. No clarifying edit exists.

## 2. Bead premise is factually wrong about the current code

Bead says: "handle_space_query in chat-server/src/space.rs runs the backend query and returns full Space objects in the matching ids set."

Actual code at `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:307-324` returns only `ids` per RFC 8620 §5.5:

```rust
let mut resp = json!({
    "accountId": account_id.as_ref(),
    "queryState": result.query_state.as_ref(),
    "canCalculateChanges": result.can_calculate_changes,
    "position": result.position,
    "ids": result.ids.iter().map(|id| id.as_ref()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
});
```

There are no "fields" to trim in the current `/query` response.

## 3. Bead acceptance text conflates /query and /get

> "The trim respects the existing `properties` request param: if the client asked for `roles` and we're returning a non-member preview, the response's `notFound` does NOT include the Space id, but the returned object omits the `roles` field"

The `properties` request param and `notFound` response field are RFC 8620 §5.1 `/get` concepts, NOT `/query`. `/query` has no `properties`, no `notFound`, no "returned object".

The bead's "Out of scope" line — "isPubliclyPreviewable enforcement on Space/get (separate from /query; would be a new bead if needed)" — is also ambiguous: it could mean (a) the field trim does NOT belong on /get, or (b) the *visibility/notFound* enforcement does not (i.e., the field trim DOES belong on /get).

## Two coherent implementations exist, and they're incompatible

**Interpretation A — literal bead text, /query deviates from RFC 8620:**
- `/query` response gains a new non-standard `spaces` (or similar) field carrying embedded Space objects.
- For non-member callers in an `isPublic: true` filter context, the embedded objects are trimmed to the spec-listed 8 fields.
- For member callers, full Space objects are embedded.
- Spec writer chooses the new response-shape field name.
- Implementation cost: medium; one new response field, per-id membership check + projection.

**Interpretation B — /get is the natural home, RFC 8620 unchanged:**
- `/query` is unchanged: returns ids per RFC 8620.
- `/get` learns the trim: for non-member callers, when the Space has `isPubliclyPreviewable: true`, return only the 8 spec-listed fields; respect the request `properties` intersection.
- For non-isPubliclyPreviewable spaces, non-member callers get the id in `notFound` (this is the "isPubliclyPreviewable enforcement" the bead defers — would be a follow-up bead).
- Implementation cost: medium; per-id check in /get handler + trim.

Interpretation B matches Mark's prior comment hint ("the trim is more naturally placed on `Space/get`") and stays RFC 8620-compliant. Interpretation A matches the bead's literal handler-name reference.

## What I need to make the call

One of:

  - **Pick A** — confirm /query deviates from RFC 8620 and tell me the response-shape field name to use, OR
  - **Pick B** — re-word bead acceptance to target `Space/get`, and confirm the "isPubliclyPreviewable enforcement" exclusion only blocks the notFound-for-non-previewable-spaces follow-up (not the field trim itself), OR
  - **Pick C** — the spec text on line 1182 was sloppy; clarify the spec first, then file a fresh bead matching the clarified spec.

The TestCallerCtx work in `tests/common/mod.rs` (the Option-1 plumbing) is the same regardless of A/B/C, but writing it in isolation without the rest of the bead leaves dead code with no consumer, so I'd rather batch it with whichever surface lands.

Releasing the claim; picking up the next non-human ready bead.
